answers.note: Thorough, well-sequenced plan with separate pre-meetings, clear ground rules, full restorative question set, a signed agreement and two-stage follow-up, plus safeguarding and online checks (parents not mentioned).

Strong, practical plan covering willingness and calm checks, the restorative questions, written repair agreement, a one-week check-in and involvement of parents, safeguarding and the year team on the online element.
Sound but thin outline with separate meetings and the right questions, yet it sets no ground rules for the joint conversation and the joint meeting itself is barely planned.

Excellent coaching-led plan with timings that sum to 20 minutes, a live blank-page recall demo that shows why rereading is weak, a specific student-chosen action and an agreed next date with a record template.
Well timed and student-led, but it explicitly tells the mentor not to explain why active methods beat rereading and only touches her goals briefly near the end.
Strong coaching questions and a well-timed retrieval experiment with a clear explanation, though the follow-up is only 'next time' with no agreed date.
Covers all three themes with purposeful, varied daily activities and practical habits, but sessions have no timings and several are overstuffed or need scenario cards the tutor must make.
Highly runnable plan with a consistent daily shape, inline scripts and scenarios and strong belonging elements, though several timed breakdowns add to 13 or 14 rather than 15 minutes.
Generic template where many sessions (current events, careers) drift off the three requested themes, with few concrete habits and weekly reading extracts and news stories the tutor must source.
